status: Individually reviewed candidate; public only after release verification
shape: Selected thick, rounded and irregular clavate stromata are distinct from slender X. hypoxylon. The first draft had pointed caps and conspicuous horizontal corrugations that disagreed with the photographed cortex. Rounded dome transitions and reduced radial oscillation corrected those defects. A prepared section is visibly open toward the default camera.
surface: Dark numerical grain and small ostiolar papilla cues give a rougher cortex. The primary section photographs show immersed perithecia rather than protruding black eggs: the first 3D lump cues were replaced by flat section-wall cues with pale lumina, and their clearance was corrected after crescent-shaped occlusion was seen.
movement: The supporting stromata and wood retain their geometry and position while enlarged teaching dots drift near selected external ostioles. The two sampled times show the same body with different overlay positions; there is no fungal walking, body waving or mature-body scaling.
residual: The clubs and contextual wood remain too regular and partly stylized. Fine cortex cracking, perithecial placement, basal mycelium, scattering and moisture response are incomplete. Section walls are flat ring cues, not reconstructed flask-shaped cavities, asci or actual tissue thickness. Their placement and count are authored. Close anatomy views show partial regions and clip some whole-body extent; the front view occludes other stromata. No developmental, discharge, airflow or physiological mechanism is computed.
assessment: Qualitative author assessment, not an accuracy score or independent scientific certification
